mainTopic: Where the laws of חוץ לזמנו, חוץ למקומו and נותר come from: which פסוק teaches each, which carries כרת, and רבא's reading of the whole long פסוק (ויקרא 7:18).
overview: The גמרא finishes showing that the extra פסוק in ויקרא 19:7 teaches חוץ למקומו, and that the כרת in the next פסוק belongs to נותר, not to חוץ למקומו. It asks why the כרת is not given the other way around. It first answers that נותר is more like חוץ לזמנו (ז"ב), but אדרבה shows that חוץ למקומו is like it in even more ways (מקד"ש). So רבי יוחנן, quoting זבדי בר לוי, brings a firm source: a גזירה שוה of 'קדש'–'קדש' ties the כרת פסוק to נותר. The גמרא then asks why the long פסוק (ויקרא 7:18) is read as חוץ לזמנו and the קדושים פסוק as חוץ למקומו, and not the reverse. Here too the similarity argument is turned around with אדרבה. So רבא says all these laws come from the long פסוק alone, and he reads it phrase by phrase. 'האכל יאכל' covers eating by a person and by the מזבח. 'זבח שלמיו' sets which offerings are included, and 'שלישי' teaches חוץ לזמנו. 'לא ירצה' teaches that פגול needs all the מתירין to be offered, 'המקריב' teaches that the disqualification happens at the offering, and 'אותו' teaches that only the offering is disqualified, not the כהן. His reading of 'לא יחשב' continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Moving the extra פסוק over to teach חוץ למקומו
steps.stepSummary: Since the פסוק cannot be teaching חוץ לזמנו, which is already known, it is applied to חוץ למקומו.
steps.simpleTranslation: If this פסוק is not needed for the case of 'beyond its time,' use it for the case of 'outside its place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof that the פסוק in ויקרא 19:7 is really about חוץ למקומו. It uses the rule that an extra פסוק gets moved to a different topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוץ לזמנו is already taught by another פסוק, so this one would be extra if it taught the same thing. The תורה does not repeat itself for nothing. So the extra פסוק is given a new job: teaching that חוץ למקומו also makes the קרבן invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for this topic, a rule for moving an extra פסוק to another topic
Apply it to the topic of
Intending, during the עבודה, to eat the קרבן after its proper time
Intending, during the עבודה, to eat the קרבן outside its proper place

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases here are about wrong intentions during the עבודה. Nobody actually ate the meat late or in the wrong place. Do not mix them up with actually eating it.

phrases.english: If it is not needed for the matter of 'beyond its time,'
phrases.notes: The פסוק being discussed is ויקרא 19:7, 'ואם האכל יאכל ביום השלישי פגול הוא.'

phrases.english: apply it to the matter of 'outside its place';

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְחוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ, תְּנֵהוּ לְעִנְיַן חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a derivation that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra פסוק in ויקרא 19:7 teaches that חוץ למקומו makes the קרבן invalid.

steps.title: The כרת in the next פסוק goes to נותר, not to חוץ למקומו
steps.stepSummary: The words 'ואכליו עונו ישא' are read as giving כרת for נותר, which leaves חוץ למקומו without כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה limited the punishment to נותר: 'whoever eats it shall bear his iniquity.' This leaves out חוץ למקומו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why חוץ למקומו has no כרת, even though it sits right next to a פסוק that mentions כרת. It says that the כרת is about נותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויקרא 19:8 mentions כרת. You might think it continues the topic of 19:7, which is now חוץ למקומו. The גמרא says instead that this כרת belongs to נותר, actually eating meat after its time. So חוץ למקומו makes the קרבן invalid, but it carries no כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה limited or excluded
Meat of a קרבן left over past its time and then eaten
'And whoever eats it shall bear his iniquity'
To exclude

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the הלכה that a קרבן made פסול by חוץ למקומו carries no כרת, unlike פיגול of חוץ לזמנו.

phrases.english: And the Merciful One limited it to נותר:
phrases.notes: 'It' means the punishment of כרת mentioned in that פסוק.

phrases.english: 'And whoever eats it shall bear his iniquity'
to exclude 'outside its place.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the second half of the derivation: who gets כרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כרת in ויקרא 19:8 applies to נותר and not to חוץ למקומו.

steps.title: Why not give כרת to חוץ למקומו and take it from נותר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק is not read the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead that 'whoever eats it shall bear his iniquity' is about חוץ למקומו, and it excludes נותר from כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 2. It asks why we did not flip the assignment of כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could just as easily continue the topic of חוץ למקומו from the פסוק before it. Then חוץ למקומו would have כרת and נותר would not. Step 2 has not explained why its reading is better.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead, an opening for an alternative reading
Spiritual cutting off, a punishment from Heaven

phrases.english: But say:
'And whoever eats it shall bear his iniquity'
this is 'outside its place,'
and it comes to exclude נותר from כרת!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: וְאֹכְלָיו עֲוֹנוֹ יִשָּׂא זֶהוּ חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assignment of כרת in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ויקרא 19:8 gives כרת to נותר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could equally be read the reverse way, so step 2's choice needs a reason.

steps.title: נותר is more like חוץ לזמנו, so it should get the כרת
steps.stepSummary: It makes more sense to give כרת to נותר. Then the גזירה שוה of 'עון' carries כרת over to חוץ לזמנו, which is similar to it in ז"ב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is more reasonable to give נותר the כרת, so that we can learn 'עון'/'עון' for חוץ לזמנו, since it resembles it in ז"ב: זמן and במה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Whichever case gets כרת will pass it on to חוץ לזמנו through a word link, and נותר is the better match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'עון' appears both here and in the פסוק of חוץ לזמנו. That link, a גזירה שוה, will give חוץ לזמנו כרת as well. A גזירה שוה fits best between similar cases. נותר and חוץ לזמנו share two features: both are about time (זמן), and both apply even on a private altar (במה).

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason
To establish, to apply the פסוק to
A גזירה שוה built on the shared word 'iniquity'
Since it resembles it
זמן (time) and במה (private altar): the two shared features

phrases.english: It stands to reason
that the פסוק should place נותר under כרת
so we can derive 'iniquity'-'iniquity' for 'beyond its time,'
phrases.notes: The פסוק about חוץ לזמנו, ויקרא 7:18, also says 'עון' ('עונה תשא'). That shared word is the link.

phrases.english: since it resembles it in ז"ב.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא נוֹתָר הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְאוֹקוֹמֵי בְּכָרֵת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reasoning from similarity: the better match for the גזירה שוה wins.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either נותר or חוץ למקומו could be the one with כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: נותר gets כרת because it shares זמן and במה with חוץ לזמנו.

steps.title: On the contrary: חוץ למקומו is more like חוץ לזמנו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. חוץ למקומו shares four features with חוץ לזמנו (מקד"ש), so maybe it should get the כרת instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! It should give חוץ למקומו the כרת, so that we can learn 'עון'/'עון' for חוץ לזמנו, since it resembles it in מקד"ש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 4 with a stronger set of similarities on the other side. The next step answers this with a new source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוץ למקומו and חוץ לזמנו are both wrong intentions (מחשבה). Both make the whole קרבן invalid even when the intention was about only part of it (קצת). Both can happen during the blood services (דם). Both are connected to an extra mention of the third day (שלישי). That is four shared features against נותר's two. So the reasoning of step 4 seems to point the other way.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary, which turns the previous argument around
מחשבה, קצת, דם, שלישי: the four shared features

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not settle the matter. It is a push-back. In the next step (step 6), the גמרא drops the similarity argument and brings a גזירה שוה instead.

phrases.english: On the contrary!

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְאוֹקוֹמֵי בְּכָרֵת –
phrases.english: the פסוק should place 'outside its place' under כרת
so we can derive 'iniquity'-'iniquity' for 'beyond its time,'
since it resembles it in מקד"ש!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה! חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְאוֹקוֹמֵי בְּכָרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the similarity argument of step 4 around.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 4 that נותר is the better match for חוץ לזמנו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חוץ למקומו shares four features (מקד"ש) with חוץ לזמנו, more than נותר's two (ז"ב), so it seems the better match for the גזירה שוה.

steps.title: A word-link shows the כרת verse is about נותר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting זבדי בר לוי, uses a גזירה שוה of 'קדש'–'קדש' to prove that the כרת in ויקרא 19:8 is talking about נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said that זבדי בר לוי taught: we learn it from the word 'sacred' appearing in two places. Here it says 'he has profaned the sacred thing of ה׳, and that soul shall be cut off.' There it says 'you shall burn the leftover in fire… because it is sacred.' Just as there it is talking about נותר, so too here it is talking about נותר.
steps.whatsHappening: The previous approach just ran into trouble, so the גמרא drops it and brings a new, firmer source. It proves that the כרת verse in פרשת קדושים is about נותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, giving כרת to נותר was only described as 'making more sense,' and step 5 challenged it with מקד"ש. Now the גזירה שוה of 'קדש'–'קדש' ties the verse straight to נותר, so this is no longer a judgment call. The verse is assigned by a fixed tradition, not by weighing which case is more similar.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from, meaning it is learned from
A link between two פסוקים that use the same word, so a law from one applies to the other
Sacred, holy. This is the shared word that links the two פסוקים
Leftover sacrificial meat that stayed past its permitted time
And it (the soul) shall be cut off. This is the word for כרת

steps.whyThisMatters: Because the verse is tied to נותר by a גזירה שוה, the challenge from מקד"ש in step 5 loses its force.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan said:
Zavdi bar Levi taught:
It is learned from "sacred" and "sacred";
It is written here:
"He has profaned the sacred thing of ה׳, and [that soul] shall be cut off,"
and it is written there:
"And you shall burn the leftover in fire, etc.";
phrases.notes: שמות 29:34. The word 'קדש' shows up in the part covered by 'etc.': 'כי קדש הוא.'

phrases.english: just as there it is talking about leftover,
so too here it is talking about leftover.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, תָּנֵי זַבְדִּי בַּר לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reasoning-based assignment that step 5 challenged with a textual גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source replaces a weakened logical argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the כרת verse could be about חוץ למקומו, since it shares מקד"ש with חוץ לזמנו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה 'קדש'–'קדש' fixes the כרת verse on נותר.

steps.title: The limiting words leave חוץ למקומו without כרת
steps.stepSummary: Since the verse is about נותר, the words 'ואכליו עונו ישא' limit its כרת to נותר and exclude חוץ למקומו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תורה limited, regarding נותר, 'and those who eat it shall bear his sin,' to exclude חוץ למקומו from כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the result of the new source. Since the verse is about נותר, its limiting words keep חוץ למקומו from getting כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ואכליו' ('those who eat IT') points only to נותר, the subject the גזירה שוה gave the verse. So חוץ למקומו still makes the offering פסול, but there is no כרת for eating it.

keyTerms.meaning: Limited or excluded, meaning the Torah narrowed the law
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳
To exclude
Intending to eat the offering outside its proper place
Being 'cut off,' a heavenly punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Excluding חוץ למקומו from כרת does not mean the offering is valid. It is still פסול; only the punishment of כרת is missing.

phrases.english: And the Merciful One limited, regarding leftover,
"And those who eat it shall bear his sin":
to exclude outside its place from כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the result of the גזירה שוה to bring back the exclusion from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוץ למקומו is פסול but carries no כרת.

steps.title: Why not switch the two verses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the two verses and asks why the long verse is read as חוץ לזמנו and the 'third day' verse in קדושים as חוץ למקומו, rather than the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what made you decide that the long verse is about חוץ לזמנו, and the 'third day' verse in פרשת 'קדושים תהיו' is about חוץ למקומו? I could switch them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about how the two verses were assigned. Why does each verse get the case it was given?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both verses talk about eating on the third day, so either could be about time or about place. The challenger says nothing forces the current assignment, so it could just as well be reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? Meaning: why did you choose this way?
The long verse
Intending to eat the offering after its proper time
The Torah section that starts 'You shall be holy'
I will reverse it

phrases.english: And what did you see
that the long verse is about outside its time,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:18, the long verse about eating on the third day.

phrases.english: and the "third" day of the section "You shall be holy"
is about outside its place?
I could reverse them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the basic two-verse setup and questions how each verse was assigned.
steps.kashyaTarget: Assigning the long verse to חוץ לזמנו and the 'third day' verse to חוץ למקומו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both verses fit either case equally, so the assignment looks arbitrary.

steps.title: The long verse fits חוץ לזמנו because it learns from נותר
steps.stepSummary: The long verse is read as חוץ לזמנו because it has the word 'עון,' which links it to נותר. חוץ לזמנו is the case similar to נותר in ז"ב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the long verse is about חוץ לזמנו, since it learns 'sin'–'sin' from נותר, which is similar to it in ז"ב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the current assignment is the logical one. The long verse should hold the case that can learn כרת from נותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The long verse says 'עונה תשא' and the נותר verse says 'עונו ישא,' so a גזירה שוה of 'עון'–'עון' passes כרת from נותר to the long verse. The case that should get it is חוץ לזמנו, because it resembles נותר in the two features abbreviated ז"ב. So the long verse is about time, and the 'third day' verse in קדושים is left for place.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it is logical
Learns, derives
Sin. This is the shared word for the גזירה שוה
Is similar to it
Short form for the two features that חוץ לזמנו and נותר share

phrases.english: It makes sense that the long verse is about outside its time,
since it learns "sin"–"sin" from leftover,
which is similar to it in ז"ב.
phrases.notes: ז"ב is a short memory tag for the two ways חוץ לזמנו and נותר are alike, mentioned earlier on this page.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'reverse it' challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical preference based on a fitting גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two verses could be switched freely.
steps.terutzMaskana: The long verse, which contains 'עון,' must be חוץ לזמנו, since that case is similar to נותר in ז"ב and learns כרת from it.

steps.title: On the contrary: flip which verse is which
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the previous answer. You could just as easily say the long verse is about חוץ למקומו and the קדושים verse is about חוץ לזמנו, because חוץ לזמנו is the one similar to נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Say the long verse is about intent to eat outside its place, and the 'third day' verse in 'You shall be holy' is about intent to eat beyond its time. Since that case is similar to נותר, the תורה placed it right next to נותר, and the words 'whoever eats it shall bear his iniquity' exclude it from כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer upside down. The same 'similar to נותר' logic could make חוץ לזמנו the case without כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said the long verse is about חוץ לזמנו, so that חוץ לזמנו, which is similar to נותר in ז"ב, can learn כרת from נותר through 'עון'–'עון'. Now the גמרא uses that same similarity the opposite way. The 'third day' verse in קדושים sits right next to the נותר verse, so the case that resembles נותר (חוץ לזמנו) belongs there. Then 'ואכליו עונו ישא' would limit the כרת to נותר and take it away from חוץ לזמנו. So the 'similar to נותר' argument cuts both ways and proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite reading makes more sense
The 'long verse' (ויקרא 7:18)
He (the Torah) placed it next to it
Excludes; limits a law so it does not apply

steps.confusionAlert: Don't lose track of which verse is which: the 'long verse' is ויקרא 7:18, and the 'third day' verse in קדושים is ויקרא 19:7, right before the נותר verse (19:8). The אדרבה swaps the earlier assignment.

phrases.english: On the contrary!
The long verse is about intent outside its place,
and the 'third' of 'You shall be holy' is about intent beyond its time,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:7, the verse just before the נותר verse.

phrases.english: because it is similar to it,
the Torah placed it next to it, and it excludes it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 9's reason for reading the long verse as חוץ לזמנו.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 9's reading of the long verse as חוץ לזמנו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'similar to נותר' reasoning can be flipped, so חוץ לזמנו is the case that belongs next to נותר and loses כרת.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole assignment of verses from steps 8 and 9
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The similarity to נותר supports the opposite assignment just as well, so it settles nothing.

steps.title: רבא: everything comes from the long verse
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops the two-verse approach and says all these laws come from the long verse. The double phrase 'האכל יאכל' teaches two kinds of eating: by a person and by the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: all of them come from the long verse. As it is written, 'be at all eaten'. The verse speaks of two eatings: one is eating by a person, and one is eating by the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a fresh answer: one verse is the source for all the laws here. He starts by explaining the doubled word 'האכל יאכל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting the laws between two verses kept running into the 'on the contrary' problem. So רבא reads everything out of ויקרא 7:18. The doubled verb shows that wrong intent about either kind of 'eating' makes פגול: a person eating the meat, or the מזבח 'eating' (burning) the offering's parts.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them (all these laws)
'Be at all eaten': a doubled verb in ויקרא 7:18
Eating by a person
'Eating' by the altar, meaning burning on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why intent to burn the parts on the מזבח at the wrong time also creates פגול, not only intent for a person to eat at the wrong time.

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said:
All of them come from the long verse;
as it is written: 'be at all eaten'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:18. The verb is said twice, and רבא learns from the doubling.

phrases.english: the verse speaks of two eatings,
one is eating by a person
and one is eating by the altar.
phrases.notes: The מזבח 'eats' when the offering's parts are burned on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the אדרבה defeated the two-verse split, רבא gives a new single-verse source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source: everything is learned from one verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The laws had to be split between two verses, and that led to an unresolvable 'which verse is which' debate.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the laws come from ויקרא 7:18, starting with 'האכל יאכל' covering both kinds of eating.

steps.title: Like שלמים: offerings with a part that makes פגול and a part that becomes פגול
steps.stepSummary: From 'מבשר זבח שלמיו', רבא learns that the law covers every offering that, like שלמים, has something that makes it פגול and something that becomes פגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Of the flesh of his peace offering': just as שלמים have something that makes פגול and something that becomes פגול, so too anything that has something that makes פגול and something that becomes פגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues reading the long verse phrase by phrase. This phrase sets the range of offerings that פגול applies to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים have blood, whose service with wrong intent makes the offering פגול, and meat, which becomes פגול. רבא uses שלמים as the model: any offering built the same way, with a 'maker' part and a part that is 'made פגול', falls under this law.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offering
Things that make an offering פגול (like the blood service)
Things that become פגול (like the meat)

phrases.english: 'Of the flesh of his peace offering'
just as שלמים have what makes פגול and what becomes פגול,
phrases.notes: In שלמים, the blood makes it פגול and the meat becomes פגול.

phrases.english: so too anything that has what makes פגול and what becomes פגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's phrase-by-phrase reading of the long verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פגול applies to every offering that, like שלמים, has a part that makes it פגול and a part that becomes פגול.

steps.title: 'Third' teaches חוץ לזמנו
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the word 'שלישי' (third day) in the long verse as the source for intent beyond its time.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Third': this is intent beyond its time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא ties the word 'third' in the long verse to חוץ לזמנו. His reading of the verse is still in progress.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים may be eaten only for two days, so 'the third day' is the time after the allowed time. That makes 'שלישי' a natural source for intent to eat beyond its time. In רבא's approach, this comes from the long verse itself, not from the verse in קדושים.

keyTerms.meaning: Third (day), the day after the allowed time for שלמים
Intent to eat or burn beyond the allowed time

steps.whatToRemember: In רבא's approach, the long verse (ויקרא 7:18) is the source: 'האכל יאכל' gives two kinds of eating, 'מבשר זבח שלמיו' sets which offerings are included, and 'שלישי' gives חוץ לזמנו.

phrases.english: 'Third'
this is intent beyond its time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's reading of the long verse with the next phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'שלישי' in ויקרא 7:18 is the source for חוץ לזמנו.

steps.title: An offering becomes פגול only when it would otherwise have been accepted
steps.stepSummary: From 'לא ירצה', רבא learns that an invalid offering becomes פגול at the same point a valid offering is accepted: only after all its permitting parts have been offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It shall not be accepted': the way a valid offering is accepted is the way an invalid one is 'accepted.' A valid offering is not accepted until all the parts that make it permitted have been offered. So too, an invalid offering does not become פגול until all the parts that make it permitted have been offered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues explaining the long verse word by word. Here he uses 'לא ירצה' to teach when an offering becomes פגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says the offering 'will not be accepted', so פגול is tied to the moment of acceptance. A valid offering is accepted only after all its מתירין, mainly the blood service, are done properly. So a wrong thought makes the offering פגול only if all the מתירין were also done, as they would be for a valid offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Acceptance: the offering doing its job and being accepted
Valid, fit
Invalid, disqualified
Permitting parts: the parts of the service, mainly the blood, that make the offering permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known rule that פגול happens only if all the מתירין were offered in the proper way.

phrases.english: "It shall not be accepted":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:18, the long verse רבא has been working through.

phrases.english: like the acceptance of a valid offering, so is the acceptance of an invalid one;
and just as the acceptance of a valid offering
does not happen until they offer all its permitting parts,
phrases.notes: Mainly the blood service, the step that makes the offering permitted.

phrases.english: so too the acceptance of an invalid offering
does not happen until they offer all its permitting parts.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״לֹא יֵרָצֶה״ – כְּהַרְצָאַת כָּשֵׁר, כֵּן הַרְצָאַת פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's word-by-word reading of the long verse after 'שלישי'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An offering becomes פגול only if all its מתירין were offered, just like a valid offering is accepted only after all its מתירין are offered.

steps.title: The disqualification happens at the time of offering
steps.stepSummary: From 'המקריב', רבא learns that the offering becomes פסול at the time it is offered, because of the wrong thought. It does not become פסול only when the third day comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He who offers': it becomes disqualified at the time of offering, and it is not disqualified on the third day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the word 'המקריב' in the verse. He uses it to show when the disqualification actually happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the verse sounds like it means someone who actually eats the meat on the third day. 'המקריב' shows the problem starts at the offering itself, through the wrong intent. So the offering is ruined from the start, even if nobody ever eats it late.

keyTerms.meaning: Offering: doing the service of the קרבן
Becomes disqualified
On the third day

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the offering was fine and only went bad when the third day came. According to רבא, the wrong thought during the offering already ruins it right then.

phrases.english: "He who offers":
it becomes disqualified at the time of offering,
and it does not become disqualified on the third day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next word in the same verse; it adds when the disqualification takes effect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פגול takes effect at the moment of offering through wrong intent, not on the third day itself.

steps.title: The offering is disqualified, not the כהן
steps.stepSummary: From 'אותו', רבא learns that the verse is talking about the offering becoming disqualified. It is not talking about the כהן being disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It': the verse is speaking about the offering, and it is not speaking about the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the word 'אותו' ('it'). He uses it to show who or what gets disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the verse says 'המקריב', one might think the כהן who offered with a wrong thought is himself made unfit. The word 'אותו' points back to the offering. So only the קרבן is ruined, and the כהן stays fit to serve.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal offering
The verse is speaking about
The priest who does the service

steps.whatToRemember: From the long verse רבא has now learned: 'האכל יאכל' teaches two kinds of eating, 'זבח שלמיו' tells which offerings, 'שלישי' tells the type of thought, 'לא ירצה' teaches that all מתירין must be offered, 'המקריב' teaches that it happens at the offering, and 'אותו' teaches that the offering is disqualified, not the כהן.

phrases.english: "It":
the verse is speaking about the offering,
and it is not speaking about the priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question that could come up from 'המקריב': does the person offering also become unfit?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wrong intent disqualifies the offering only, not the כהן who offered it.

steps.title: Starting the next phrase: 'it shall not be credited'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the verse, 'לא יחשב', to begin explaining it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the next words of the verse, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא is continuing his order through the verse. Nothing new is taught yet; the phrase is only opened here, and its lesson follows on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall not be credited / counted
Thought, intent: the root of the word יחשב

phrases.english: "It shall not be credited":

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the same verse.
